models_evaluated: Basque Country Prospective Complications and Mortality Study risk engine

links.outcome: Need for local recalibration of CVD risk models in a Spanish T2D cohort
links.effect: All models showed good calibration, but most required recalibration; ADVANCE-, DIAL2-, and SCORE2-related models did not.
links.quote: All models showed good calibration, although most of them required recalibration, with the exception of ADVANCE-, DIAL2-, and SCORE2-related models.

links.outcome: Comparative discrimination and calibration of 18 candidate risk scores on the same local cohort
links.effect: Discrimination was moderate for all models. Diabetes-specific models and general-population models with HbA1c performed better; DIAL2, DIAL2-extended, SCORE2-diabetes, and ADVANCE had optimal calibration without recalibration.
links.quote: In our context, models derived for or adapted to diabetes patients, as well as models derived in the general population but incorporating diabetes-related metabolic measures (such as Hb1Ac) as predictors, demonstrated better performance than the others.
